physics_checks.expected_check: For a 4318 W heat load with typical EGW flow rates, 112.5 K is plausible only if flow is severely restricted or area is undersized. The ±50 K uncertainty makes this unusable for design decisions.
physics_checks.why: The uncertainty band is 57% of nominal. No engineer can size a cooling system with this. The pressure drop of 28501.9 Pa (~0.285 bar) is high and suggests the assumed geometry is restrictive. Without CFD or bench data, both the heat transfer coefficient and pressure drop are guesses.

physics_checks.expected_check: For a laminated bus bar in a SiC inverter, sub-10 nH is achievable but depends entirely on geometric overlap, dielectric thickness, and terminal geometry. The 2.4x range (4.15 to 9.9) is unacceptable.
physics_checks.why: The nominal value is physically plausible but the range is too wide. Without supplier terminal geometry and 3D extraction, this is a geometry assumption, not a measurement. SiC switches at high di/dt; ESL error of 3.5 nH changes overshoot voltage significantly.

physics_checks.expected_check: For a Formula E MGU at peak power (~350 kW), inverter losses at ~2% would be ~7 kW. Motor losses could add 3-5 kW. 4318 W seems low for peak operation or may represent a specific duty point not stated.
physics_checks.why: No duty cycle, operating point, or loss breakdown is provided. 4318 W without context is meaningless. If this is continuous rating, it may be reasonable. If peak, it is dangerously low. The provenance is ANALYTICAL_FROM_ASSUMED_GEOMETRY with no loss map backing it.

physics_checks.expected_check: ~0.285 bar is high for a cold plate. Typical automotive cold plates run 0.05–0.15 bar. This suggests either tiny channels or assumed geometry that is not representative.
physics_checks.why: Analytical from assumed geometry. No CFD, no bench measurement. The high pressure drop may force a larger pump, adding mass and parasitic load — neither of which is tracked.
